schedule.title: Are We Awake?
schedule.description:
"Are We Awake?" is a five-track EP listen — Funky House / Deep n Funky, 124–127 BPM. SERGIK wrote it as one room, start to finish. It opens on It Is What It Is: carries its title like a verdict. Space opens into Elevator Musik: moves like a system running just slightly off its own schematics. The sequence holds through No Stopping: earns its title the moment the kick arrives — not with force, but with the kind of inevitability that makes you stop checking your watch. The energy lifts into OG Coconut - What you want (SERGIK x OG Coconut), which arrives with a question it never quite finishes asking — and that unresolved tension is exactly the point. This is the peak of the listen. It lands on Whats the Reason, which doesn't ask the question gently — it plants it in the room and lets the breakbeat do the interrogating. Play it in order — a D# major breakbeat that asks something the 808 never quite resolves — bright enough to pull you in, broken enough to keep you honest.

2. Elevator Musik
3. No Stopping

schedule.title: In The Streets
schedule.description: "In The Streets" is a five-track EP listen — Funky House / Deep n Funky, 124–126 BPM. SERGIK wrote it as one room, start to finish. It opens on The Assignment: Conversation between bass and kick — bounce rather than lockstep. The sequence holds through Electrify: Awaiting audio analysis. This is the peak of the listen. Space opens into Melt: Open space so bass and delay can act as architecture. The sequence holds through They Know: Slow the felt pocket against a faster clock so attention drops into the snare and sub. It lands on In The Streets: Conversation between bass and kick — bounce rather than lockstep. Play it in order. The titles already tell you where the room is going.

It lands on The World Dont Stop The Night: Conversation between bass and kick — bounce rather than lockstep. Play it in order. The titles already tell you where the room is going.

schedule.title: UTOPIA
schedule.description:
"UTOPIA" is a five-track EP listen — Reggae / Dub Reggae, 126–182 BPM. SERGIK wrote it as one room, start to finish. It opens on Utopia, which arrives the way a held breath releases — slowly, with weight. The energy lifts into Like The Ol Days (Bass VIP), which doesn't ask for your attention — it pulls it low, into the chest. The energy lifts into Jahdelicah: 1 doesn't march — it sways. The sequence holds through Man On A Journey: moves the way conviction does — unhurried but impossible to ignore. It closes on Subliminal acid, which arrives at a sprint — 182 BPM on the clock — yet somehow the body reads it as a slow, pressurised exhale. Play it in order — a D# minor pressure system — dub architecture at a steppers tempo, where silence and sub do equal work.

schedule.title: Staying A Vibe
schedule.description: "Staying A Vibe" is a five-track EP listen — Soulful House / Deep n Funky, 124–126 BPM. SERGIK wrote it as one room, start to finish. It opens on Pre Party, which arrives already moving — a low-slung F minor groove that doesn't announce itself so much as pull you in by the shoulders. The energy lifts into Tequila Power: runs deep before it runs loud. The sequence holds through Hydrate, which lands in E major with a warmth you feel before you've made a decision about it. The energy lifts into Mind n Body: settles into D minor with a patience that most records don't bother with. It closes on Last Night, which arrives in A# major with a brightness that doesn't announce itself — it just lifts the room by a degree or two before anyone decides to let it. Play it in order — late-night warmth that moves before the room knows it agreed to.

schedule.title: Soul Candy
schedule.description:
“Soul Candy” is a Deep House EP infused with funky grooves and soulful melodies, crafted to elevate any moment. Whether you’re unwinding after a long day, vibing at a house party, or cruising through the city, this EP delivers feel-good energy and uplifting beats that blend groove, emotion, and rhythm. Perfect for turning any situation into a soulful escape.

This EP took about a year to come together. Out of all the music I made during that time, these five tracks were chosen and curated to tell a real story—through sound.

It starts with Soul Candy—something sweet for the soul. That healing type of energy. A pause in the noise.

Everyday Gratitude came from slowing down and appreciating the little things—waking up, light through the window, just being present.

Spring Swing is that shift from cold to warm. A bloom. That change in energy when life starts to feel light, colorful, and full of beauty again.

Back to the Basics was me grounding myself—returning to what really matters and stripping it all down to the core.

And All of the Vibes is the full-circle moment. The celebration of everything I felt along the way. Free, honest, and flowing.

Dropped it on Valentine’s Day to show love—to life, the people around me, and everything that makes it all worth it. It’s about growth, change, peace, and appreciation.

schedule.title: FTP
schedule.description:
"FTP" is a five-track EP listen — House / Detroit Techno, 120 BPM. Sergik wrote it as one room, start to finish. It opens on FTP: The title track arrives like a statement of purpose — not a question, not a pitch, just the floor opening up beneath you. The sequence holds through The Worst: There is something almost confrontational about the way 'The Worst' refuses to ornament itself. The sequence holds through One Of Those Nights: There is a particular kind of night that 'One Of Those Nights' already knows — the one where the room stops being a collection of strangers and becomes something else en. The sequence holds through Dmn8r's, which is the track on FTP that doesn't ask permission. It closes on Zoned (feat. Lugh Haurie): There is a particular stillness at the centre of 'Zoned' — the kind that arrives not from emptiness but from two people locking into exactly the same idea at exactly the. Play it in order — for the room where the night stops being a sequence of songs and becomes a single, unbroken decision to remain.

schedule.title: Dumb
schedule.description:
"Dumb" arrives at 120 BPM and wastes no time making its case: a synth-bass that sits low and deliberate, offbeat hats that open space between every kick, and a backbeat that lands with the quiet confidence of a room that already knows where it's going. The track carries a Detroit bloodline in its bones — functional, no-excess, built for the long stretch of a set when the floor needs something to lean into rather than chase. There is a stillness inside the momentum here, the kind that makes four minutes feel earned.

Sergik lets the architecture do the talking. "Dumb" is not a track that announces itself; it accumulates — pulse by pulse, hat by hat — until the room has already committed without quite deciding to. That restraint is the point, and it is anything but dumb.

schedule.title: Recouperate
schedule.description:
Recouperate lands somewhere between a late-night promise and an early-morning resolution. The synth bass settles into the low end with a kind of quiet authority — tonal, unhurried, patient — while the snare holds the backbeat with enough snap to remind you where you are. There is a precision to how the track breathes: offbeat hats opening small pockets of air, the four-on-the-floor pulse keeping everything honest without ever feeling mechanical. It sits at 120 BPM and earns every second of it, drawing from the lineage where Detroit and Chicago still talk to each other through concrete walls.

This is a record that trusts the room. No grand gesture, no excessive arrangement — just a groove that settles into the body and stays there, the kind of track a DJ reaches for when the floor is already warm and the moment needs holding rather than pushing.

schedule.title: Get on my vibe
schedule.description:
There is a particular moment in a good house record where the room stops being a collection of individuals and becomes one breathing thing. 'Get on my vibe' finds that moment and holds it. Sergik builds the track around a synth-bass that sits low and deliberate beneath a kick that never wavers, letting the offbeat hats carry the social invitation — the small, open spaces between beats where bodies find each other. It is unhurried, confident, and warm in the way that Detroit and Chicago taught the world warmth could live inside a machine.

At 120 BPM the record runs at exactly the pace a crowd settles into without thinking about it — pulse meeting pulse. There is nothing surplus here. The backbeat lands where it should, the low end locks rather than wanders, and the whole architecture trusts the listener. That trust is the point.

schedule.title: This is the sound
schedule.description:
"This Is the Sound" arrives at exactly the temperature a room needs before it tips — 120 BPM, held steady, no argument. SERGIK builds from the floor up: a synth-bass that sits under the kick like ballast, offbeat hats that open a pocket just wide enough for a crowd to slip inside, and a backbeat landing on the two and four with the quiet authority of something that has always been true. There is no decoration for its own sake. The track earns its name by committing to a single, unbroken physical proposition and refusing to flinch.

The Detroit and Chicago bloodlines are audible not as reference but as posture — the confidence of a record that knows the room it was made for. What SERGIK delivers here is structural honesty: every element placed where it does the most good, every gap left open long enough to feel like an invitation. The result is a track that does not ask you to pay attention. It simply starts moving, and your body follows.
